A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same paper, InfoNCE Induces Gaussian Distribution. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A-E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original synthetic-data and CIFAR-10 experiments, plus distributional analyses of pretrained representations, with results in Tables 1-2 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses, including Gaussianity diagnostics, whitening comparisons, and augmentation-strength studies.

M1.justification: The InfoNCE formulation, encoder procedures, and entropy/norm regularized objective in Sections 3-4 are unchanged. No algorithm, loss, or model component is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic Laplace, Gaussian-mixture and binary data, CIFAR-10, MS-COCO, and ImageNet-R sketch/painting domains. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain the same comparisons: supervised versus contrastive ResNet-18, and CLIP/DINO versus supervised ResNet-34/DenseNet. The newly cited Butakov et al. work is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E.1 retain identical splits, augmentations, model configurations, training budgets, batch-size/dimension sweeps, and CV/AD/DP evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The batch-size and dimensionality analyses, ImageNet-R checks, whitening comparisons in Figures 9-10, and augmentation-strength analysis in Figure 11 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the statement that trends are stable across runs and figures show representative seeds. Run/seed information, normality-testing practices, and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 and all experimental figures retain the same numerical values, curves, and qualitative findings. No result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, alignment bound, Gaussian-limit results, and regularization analysis in Sections 3-4 are unchanged, as are the proofs and derivations in Appendices A-D.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about bounded alignment, spherical uniformity, asymptotic Gaussian structure, and empirical support.

C2.justification: The interpretations of Gaussianity, alignment saturation, whitening, and augmentation effects are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning asymptotic assumptions and the absence of optimization-dynamics guarantees.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 retains the same implementation instructions, hyperparameters, software and hardware disclosures. The reproducibility statement and code-access links are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Butakov et al. (2024), Efficient distribution matching of representations via noise-injected deep infomax, and acknowledges distribution-matching perspectives. It changes the literature-gap description from 'theoretically unexplained' to 'theoretically underexplored'; other positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The opening related-work paragraph receives localized wording edits, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The section order, main exposition, and appendix prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised paragraph reflows on page 2. The added reference shifts bibliography entries across pages 12-14 and slightly compresses appendix-overview spacing. All figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves attribution and research positioning by acknowledging distribution-matching work and using a less categorical literature-gap statement in Section 2. The benefit is limited: the technical arguments, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged.
